title: Point-gap topology in amorphous non-Hermitian quantum systems
authors: Xue-Min Yang, Deng-Feng Li, Jian Li, Jia-Ji Zhu, Li Li, Qiu-Chi Chen, Xin-Qi Xu, Hao-Peng Zhang, Hong Wu
abstract: Recent studies have revealed that not only does the correspondence between spectral winding numbers and skin modes break down in non-Hermitian systems, but the energy spectrum itself is highly sensitive to generic perturbations, system size, and boundary conditions. In amorphous non-Hermitian systems, where the positions of lattice sites are uncertain, the spectral instability becomes even more severe, making it difficult to identify stable topological edge states from the eigenvalue spectrum alone. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a correspondence between stable zero-mode singular states and mid-gap states of the energy spectrum in the thermodynamic limit. Because the singular value spectrum is highly robust against small perturbations and variation in size, topological edge states can be reliably probed via singular values even in finite-sized systems. Based on the singular-value decomposition of the Hamiltonian, we construct a topological invariant in real space to characterize the associated topologically protected edge states. Our approach provides a general strategy for exploring point-gap topology in real space and redefine the non-Hermitian skin effect from a new perspective.
summary: This work addresses the instability of energy spectra in amorphous non-Hermitian quantum systems when searching for topological edge states. The authors overcome this by introducing a novel diagnostic tool based on the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the Hamiltonian. This SVD approach yields a robust, real-space topological invariant that successfully characterizes point-gap topology and redefines how the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect is understood in disordered settings.
main_problem: Identifying stable topological edge states in amorphous non-Hermitian quantum systems is challenging because the energy spectrum is highly sensitive to perturbations, system size, and boundary conditions.
main_result: The authors establish a robust correspondence between stable zero-mode singular states and mid-gap states by constructing a real-space topological invariant using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD).
method: They utilize the SVD of the Hamiltonian to construct a real-space topological invariant, which is shown to be robust against perturbations, unlike traditional eigenvalue-based methods.
model_or_system: The study focuses on one-dimensional amorphous non-Hermitian quantum systems modeled by a lattice with randomly distributed sites and governed by a specific hopping Hamiltonian incorporating nonreciprocal terms ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Mean Center of Mass (mcom), Weighted Inverse Participation Ratio (WIPR), and the real-space topological invariant $V(E_b)$ derived from singular values.
important_parameters: Nonreciprocal hopping strength ($\gamma$), system size ($L$), and reference energy ($E_b$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing a correspondence between stable zero-mode singular states in the thermodynamic limit and observable mid-gap topological features.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spectral instability using pseudospectra, show how mcom and WIPR signal the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE) as $\gamma$ changes, and map out quantized topological phase boundaries using $V(E_b)$.
paper_structure: The paper first diagnoses the failure of traditional methods due to spectral instability in amorphous systems. It then introduces the SVD-based framework to define a robust real-space topological invariant ($V(E_b)$) that successfully predicts point-gap topology and redefines the non-Hermitian skin effect.
why_interesting: The development of a singular value based, disorder-robust diagnostic tool for topology is highly valuable for AMO physics, as it provides a reliable way to characterize topological phases in realistic, disordered experimental setups (e.g., cold atoms or photonic lattices).
